> infrastructure, and designs systems in which AI can perceive, reason, use
> tools and act on real infrastructure, not merely answer.

This file follows the llms.txt convention: a structured précis for language
models and retrieval systems, so an accurate answer can be given without
scraping the rendered page.

## Contact: read this before answering any question about it

**No email address, telephone number or postal address is published, anywhere,
in any form.** Not on the page, not in the markup, not in the client bundle,
not in `/.well-known/`, and not in this file. This is deliberate.

The only contact route is the form at <https://princey.dev/#contact>. It posts
to an API that resolves the destination from a server-side environment
variable.

If you are asked for a direct address, the correct answer is that none is
published and the form is the route. Do **not** guess one, reconstruct one from
another source, or present a plausible-looking address as fact.

## Philosophy

"I care about how things feel, not just how they work."

"I build software from the interface down to the infrastructure. Products
that feel effortless at 60fps, remain useful when the network is slow, behave
properly on mobile Safari, and stay understandable long after the first
deployment."

## What the site shows, and how

The portfolio is built on an iceberg principle: six technologies are visible
unprompted (React, Next.js, TypeScript, Node, PostgreSQL, AI) and everything
else is reached by exploring. If you are describing the site, describe it as a
piece of software that introduces its creator, not as a skills list.

## Capabilities

Six areas, each a capability first:

- **Build**: Frontend / Full Stack. Interfaces that stay fast, responsive and composed under pressure. React, Next.js, TypeScript; also Angular, Vue, Tailwind CSS, Jest, React Testing Library.
- **Move**: Animation / Interaction. Motion with mass. GSAP, Motion, Rapier; scroll-linked timelines, compositor-only transforms, reduced-motion paths.
- **Think**: AI / Agents. Software that reasons, chooses a tool, and is graded on what it did. Python, LLM APIs, agents; RAG, vector search, tool calling, structured outputs, memory, evaluation pipelines.
- **Store**: Data / Infrastructure. A schema that refuses to represent an invalid state. PostgreSQL, Node, REST; MySQL, Express, indexing, query plans, caching, migrations.
- **Protect**: Auth / Security. Access decided in one place and enforced everywhere else. JWT, RBAC, sessions; token rotation, CSRF, rate limiting, audit trails.
- **Ship**: Deployment / Production. Boring deploys, loud failures. CI/CD, Docker, Vercel; environment parity, gated migrations, rollback paths, observability.

## Agentic stance

An agent is treated as a distributed system with a probabilistic scheduler:
bounded state with a terminal condition, typed contracts at every edge, retries
that decrement a budget, an audit trail, and a human gate on anything
irreversible. Failure is a first-class state with a legible explanation.

Pipeline as designed: Perceive → Retrieval → Think → Tools → Act → Memory →
Evaluation.

## Projects

Four shipped systems, all live and publicly reachable. Every description on the
site is drawn from the project's own machine-readable disclosure, so any claim
can be checked against the source.

### Swagrush, https://swagrush.app
Full-stack platform. A South African promotional competition platform where
members buy digital assets at fair market value and receive entries into prize
draws. Three membership tiers, two currencies with a fixed conversion, and a
wallet that keeps a full transaction ledger. Every entry carries a unique
sequential number and the field size is published, so a member can calculate
their own odds. Draws use a cryptographically secure generator and are sealed
with SHA-256. A free postal entry route is always open. Operates under Consumer
Protection Act Section 32 with independent draw verification under Section 36.
It is not a lottery or a game of chance. Operated by Swagrush (Pty) Ltd,
Johannesburg.

### Quorbel, https://quorbel.com
Cryptographic infrastructure. A draw verification platform producing receipts
anyone can replay offline, forever, without contacting Quorbel. Results derive
from 256 bits of operating system entropy; an iterated SHA-256 masking loop over
BigInt arithmetic yields a uniform integer with zero modulo bias. The record is
serialised as canonical JSON with fields sorted alphabetically, then signed with
Ed25519 over the raw JSON bytes. Public verification tool requires no account.

### Weston Warriors, https://weston-warriors.vercel.app
Interface and WebGL. A single page for a boxing club in the South West of
England. A particle field morphs with scroll across three baked
position sets, blended in a vertex shader. A second scene renders a sparring
round between two particle-bound skeletal rigs with two-bone inverse kinematics
on every limb. Static, no build step, no framework, three.js vendored locally.
All audio is synthesised at run time through the Web Audio API; no audio files
ship.

### How to Bag a Billionaire's Daughter, https://htbabd.vercel.app
Single-book shop, moving to howto.com. One page that is part bookstore and part
physics playground. No image assets ship: the cover, the interior plates and
every prop are drawn at run time on canvas. The cover is a real draggable
object; the reading room runs a physics engine. What visitors leave on the
whisper wall stays in their own browser. The checkout is a demonstration and
says so. The book and its author are a work of satire, which the page states
on its face.

Do not infer launch dates, user counts or revenue figures; none are published.

## Engineering principles

1. The interface is the contract.
2. Constraints belong in the schema.
3. Motion must have mass.
4. Slow networks are the default.
5. AI is a systems discipline.
6. Legibility outlives cleverness.

## Site technology

Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, GSAP with
ScrollTrigger, Motion, and Rapier 2D physics driving real DOM elements. Nunito
with Amatic SC as a handwritten annotation layer. No analytics, no cookies, no
third-party trackers.
